    A greedy search, with a few escape routes.

    Better moves lower the cost. Sideways moves explore a plateau. Random restarts leave a stuck search behind.

    Hill Climbing Lab / An experiment in local searchBuilt for curiosity. Runs in your browser.
    THE IDEA IN A MINUTE

    Always take the better step.

    Hill climbing keeps one current state, scores its neighbors, and greedily picks a better one. This lab minimizes a cost, which is equivalent to climbing the fitness −cost.

    01

    Move toward a lower cost

    For N-Queens, one move places a single queen in another row of the same column. We check all N(N − 1) neighbors and count each attacking pair once. Zero means solved.

    02

    Meet a plateau or local minimum

    A plateau has equal-cost neighbors. A strict local minimum has only worse neighbors. A bounded number of sideways moves can explore a plateau, but may still cycle or get stuck.

    03

    Give the search a fresh start

    When no move is allowed, the search shows why it is stuck. With random restarts enabled, the next step starts a new attempt. The best state is remembered, and the restart budget bounds the run.

    About the landscape

    2D and 3D show the same function of x and y. Search evaluates up to eight neighboring points inside [−3, 3]². A neighborhood minimum depends on the step size; it does not prove a continuous or global minimum. The smooth bowl, terraces and Rastrigin have a known global minimum of 0.
